correctness.rationale: For nonempty subsets the divisor Möbius test of the joint gcd yields Σ μ(d)(2^(n/d)−1); the constants cancel only for n>1. Parity is immediate for n>1, and mod 3 the sum is zero on odd n≥3 and on 4|n; for n=2w, w>1 odd, the odd and even squarefree divisors pair to give 2Σ_{e|w}μ(e)=0. For odd m≥5 the order d of 2 is >2, so a prime p≡−1 mod d (chosen >B) has Φ(p)≡2^(-1)−2≠0 mod m. A different prime q≡1 mod lcm(T,d) makes Φ(pq)≡0 and pq≡p mod T. Dirichlet supplies arbitrarily large primes in these reduced classes. For 4|m choose p>B odd, p≡1 mod T, and Φ(p),Φ(p²) are respectively 2 and 0 mod 4, sufficient to distinguish them modulo m. Every other nondivisor of 6 has odd part ≥5. An eventual period would force equal residues at any two indices above its threshold in the same T-class. Thus the theorem is true as stated.

originality.rationale: The full Ayad–Kihel paper was recovered. Despite Theorem 3 being worded for f(n), its proof explicitly rules out eventual periodicity of Φ itself for every prime ℓ≥5, using the same prime/semiprime witnesses above any threshold. Lemma 2 gives the positive mod-3 case. The extension to every odd m≥5 is a mechanical change to the same argument (Euler's totient of m or ord_m(2) in place of ℓ−1; 2^(-1)−2=−3/2 mod m). The mod-4 case is an immediate Möbius/square-divisibility check. The exact all-moduli wording is not stated in the earlier paper; the lack of an independent mathematical remainder, not a missing publication or an exact-match assumption, determines the verdict.
residual_risks: No claim is made that the exact composite-modulus wording appears in the earlier paper. The comparison rests on the prime proof and its explicit elementary adaptation, not a literature-exhaustiveness or priority claim.
